"This chart, titled **"Inflation Persistence (Months to threshold),"** illustrates the time (in months) it took for various countries to reduce their inflation rates to specific levels (40%, 20%, and 10%) following successful stabilization programs in different years.

### Chart Components
*   **Left Y-Axis:** Measures the time in months (0 to 90).
*   **Right Y-Axis (rhs):** Measures "Starting inflation" as a percentage (0 to 300).
*   **X-Axis:** Lists six countries and the year their stabilization program began: Argentina ('91), Peru ('93), Brazil ('94), Turkey ('01), Mexico ('87), and Israel ('85).
*   **Legend:**
    *   **Light Blue Bar:** Months to reach a 40 percent inflation threshold.
    *   **Medium Blue Bar:** Months to reach a 20 percent inflation threshold.
    *   **Dark Blue Bar:** Months to reach a 10 percent inflation threshold.
    *   **Black Diamond (♦):** Starting inflation level (measured on the right-hand scale).

### Data Extraction
The following table provides estimated values based on the chart's scales:

| Country (Year) | Starting Inflation (%) [Right Axis] | Months to 40% Threshold | Months to 20% Threshold | Months to 10% Threshold |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Argentina ('91)** | ~130 | ~10 | ~14 | ~28 |
| **Peru ('93)** | ~41 | ~4 | ~16 | ~29 |
| **Brazil ('94)** | ~230 | ~15 | ~24 | ~33 |
| **Turkey ('01)** | ~43 | ~12 | ~29 | ~33 |
| **Mexico ('87)** | ~95 | ~13 | ~15 | ~64 |
| **Israel ('85)** | ~170 | ~12 | ~13 | ~84 |

### Summary of Observations
*   **Starting Inflation:** Brazil ('94) had the highest starting inflation at approximately 230%, while Peru ('93) and Turkey ('01) had the lowest among the group, both starting in the 40-45% range.
*   **Time to 10%:** While most countries reached the 10% threshold within 35 months, Mexico and Israel were notable exceptions, taking significantly longer (approximately 64 and 84 months, respectively) to reach that level.
*   **Initial Drop:** Most countries were able to drop inflation to the 40% and 20% thresholds relatively quickly (under 30 months), but the "last mile" to reach 10% inflation showed the most variance in persistence."
